output.summary: Mostly vigorous woody climbing vines, Clematis species occur chiefly in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere and rarely in the tropics. Their divided leaves have stalks that twist around supports, though some species are shrubs or herbaceous perennials. Depending on the type, flowers appear on last year's side shoots, new stem tips, or both.
output.edibilityNote: The genus can cause internal bleeding if eaten in large amounts; C. ligusticifolia seeds and acrid leaves were historically used as a pepper substitute.
